Points on the FWA network downstream of a regulating dam

Source: R/link_regulated.R
knw_link_regulated.Rd

scripts/0294's regulated-reach test. A CABD dam with a reservoir, or a degree of regulation of regulation_min percent or more, is placed on the nearest main-flow FWA segment within dam_snap_m; a point is regulated when such a dam lies upstream of it (fwa_downstream() with the roles swapped). wet's flow is natural flow, so on a regulated river it is not the flow the fish meet. A dam equally near two segments is placed on the one with the lower linear_feature_id, so every database places it alike (#161).

Usage

knw_link_regulated(conn, pts, dam_snap_m = 500, regulation_min = 10)

Arguments

conn

a DBI connection to a database holding cabd and whse_basemapping.

pts

data.frame with blue_line_key, downstream_route_measure, wscode and localcode (ltree text, as knw_link_flow() returns them).

dam_snap_m

numeric(1) how far a dam may sit from the segment it is placed on.

regulation_min

numeric(1) percent degree of regulation at or above which a dam without a reservoir counts.

Value

A list: regulated, a tibble of the distinct pts keys with a logical regulated; dams, the dams placed (cabd_id, dam_name_en, degree_of_regulation_pc, reservoir_present, position, snap_m).

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
conn <- DBI::dbConnect(RPostgres::Postgres())
f <- knw_link_flow(conn, 701747495)
knw_link_regulated(conn, data.frame(blue_line_key = 360886335, downstream_route_measure = 100,
                                    wscode = f$wscode, localcode = f$localcode))
} # }
